outcome: No result found that addresses or moves the general classification question; only continued case-by-case converse-Lyapunov work for specific restricted system classes, and unrelated AI/ML work on synthesizing Lyapunov functions for particular engineering systems.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks a meta-mathematical classification question: for which classes of ODEs does Lyapunov's second method (classical or 'canonically generalized') give necessary AND sufficient conditions for stability, not merely sufficient ones. This is a genuinely open, very broadly stated question with no dedicated Wikipedia article (confirmed by fetching en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyapunov_function, which states only that 'for certain classes of ODEs' the existence of a Lyapunov function is necessary and sufficient, without treating this as an open research programme or discussing any 2024-2026 developments). Searching the current literature turns up a large and active body of converse-Lyapunov-theorem research, but every item found is a case/variant restricted to a specific system class rather than an attempt at (or contribution to) the general characterization: a 2025 JOTA survey by Haidar and Mason, 'Converse Lyapunov Results for Uniform Stability Properties,' covers converse results for uniformly asymptotically stable systems under parametric perturbations with emphasis on infinite-dimensional systems (a restricted class, and itself a survey of existing results rather than a new general theorem); a 2025 ESAIM:COCV paper and a 2024 arXiv/Automatica paper extend converse Lyapunov results to switched systems with average dwell-time / bounded switching intervals; other 2024-2025 papers treat converse theorems for control systems with regulated cost, fixed-time input-to-state stability, and neutral/stochastic/hybrid functional differential equations. All of these narrow or extend converse theorems within an already-delimited subclass (switched systems, systems with regulated cost, etc.) — they change what a careful reader would write about that subclass, not about the general question posed in the bullet. Separately, a distinct and unrelated body of 2024-2025 work uses machine learning (reinforcement learning, symbolic regression, transformer models, e.g. 'Analytical Lyapunov Function Discovery: An RL-based Generative Approach,' ICML 2025) to numerically discover or synthesize Lyapunov functions for specific engineering control systems. This is an algorithmic/engineering search technique for exhibiting a certificate for a given system, not mathematical progress on the classification question of which classes of ODEs admit necessary-and-sufficient Lyapunov criteria in general — it does not touch the bullet's scope at all. A categorical/coalgebraic paper (arXiv:2505.22968, 'Categorical Lyapunov Stability II') proves Lyapunov and converse-Lyapunov theorems in an abstract category-theoretic framework for F-coalgebras, not for classes of ODEs, and is a different (though related) mathematical object, not a case of this problem. I found no AI involvement of any kind in the actual converse-Lyapunov-theorem papers that are mathematically closest to the bullet's scope; all such work is conventional human mathematics. Overall this is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened': the general classification problem, as Wikipedia states it, remains untouched since 26 January 2024.
competing_reading: One could argue the accumulating converse-Lyapunov results for ever-more system classes (switched systems, parametrically-perturbed infinite-dimensional systems, systems with regulated cost, fixed-time ISS, etc.) collectively constitute incremental 'progress' toward the classification the bullet asks for, since each new class for which necessity-and-sufficiency is established is one more class added to the eventual answer. Under a very generous reading this could be coded `progress` rather than `open`. I reject this reading because the bullet's question is about identifying the general boundary/characterization across all ODE classes, and no source treats these individual results as steps toward, or even discusses them in relation to, that general characterization; each is self-contained work on its own named subclass, consistent with the pattern the triage pass already identified (and with the strict §3.1 rule that a variant/case affecting only a delimited subclass, with no bearing on the general question, is not itself a change in the bullet's scope unless framed as such).
what_would_settle_it: A paper or survey that explicitly poses and answers (fully or partially, with a genuinely new general-purpose criterion) the question of which classes of ODEs admit Lyapunov's second method as necessary and sufficient for stability — as opposed to yet another converse theorem for one more named subclass — would settle whether progress has occurred. Absent that, the honest answer stays 'open, no change found.'
